_what: Names the voices of a recorded call from the call app's own screen (read-data/name-from-the-call.mjs). While a call is recorded, something reads the app's accessibility elements every moment (tools/read-what-is-on-screen or the Mac app's screen reader; elements have role, title, description, value, identifier, label) and `namesSpeaking` finds who the app shows as speaking by the first row of `apps` whose `app_contains` matches the app (a row without it matches every app). A row says which element field marks a speaker (`speaking.field` contains any of `speaking.contains_any`), how a name is cut out of it (`name.strip`, regular expressions removed, then trimmed) and how far the app's picture trails the sound (`lag_seconds`). Rows for particular call apps are added here as they are checked on the real app; none is assumed. Only turns whose voice label matches `unnamed_label` (how listening words a voice it could not name) are laid over; a voice already named is left alone. `reconcile` says: a voice takes the name shown for at least `sure_share` of the time it spoke, and at least `least_overlap_seconds` of it; a name goes to one voice only; otherwise the voice is left unnamed and its candidates are listed.
evidence: Shown as speaking by the call app on screen ({share} of the time this voice spoke, {seconds} seconds).

words.needs_turns: Give turns: [{ start, end, who }] in seconds, such as the speakers tool:who-is-in-this answered.
words.needs_samples: Give samples: [{ at, names }] or [{ at, elements }] in milliseconds from the start of the recording.
words.needs_apply: To name the voices in the person's Trillion give apply: { app, since, until }, where since and until are ISO times.
words.needs_caller: Naming the voices in the person's Trillion is done by the caller that holds the name_speaker door; this run gives the assignments only. Leave out apply.
